key_insight: PINN training can match full-space optimization within a small Hessian-eigenvector subspace selected by gradient alignment rather than curvature magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Gradient-aligned subspaces could guide more efficient optimizers for PDE-solving neural networks without requiring well-conditioned projected Hessians.
method: Compute a full eigendecomposition of the loss Hessian.
Select the dominant aligned subspace (DAS) using gradient alignment, not eigenvalue magnitude.
Restrict training to DAS with line search and extend the analysis to Gauss–Newton.
evidence_signal: Across Poisson, heat, wave, and viscous Burgers benchmarks, DAS-restricted training empirically matches full-space training even when the projected Hessian remains ill-conditioned.
watch_item: Full Hessian eigendecomposition is costly at scale, and the abstract does not establish net computational savings.
paper_title: A Systematic Analysis of a Small Optimal Subspace for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: $n$-DAS $\subset \mathbb{R}^p$
